- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.3) or shows strong reversal signals, model often underestimates or fails to anticipate sharp drops; increase forecast lows by 2–5%.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (especially if sentiment is neutral or mixed), leading to overshoots; apply a 1–3 day lag correction to peak forecasts.
- If sentiment shows strong momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive positive values), model tends to overfit trend; apply mean reversion bias: cap forecast at 1.5–2 std dev above recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misjudges early-week price behavior; adjust first 5–7 days downward if sentiment is weak or mixed.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive, model delays correction; add 1–2 day buffer to forecast rise to avoid premature overcorrection.
